header.userPrompt:
Implement worktree runs for orca: a run-level `--worktree` flag that creates a git worktree at startup and runs the whole flow inside it.

The design is already settled and written down. Read these two files first — they are in the working tree (currently untracked) and are the authority on what to build:

- docs/plans/worktree-runs/specification.md — what the feature does and why each decision was made.
- docs/plans/worktree-runs/implementation-plan.md — the concrete work, as three PRs, with verified file and line references against this commit.

Land all three of the plan's PRs as one change on this branch, in the plan's order:

1. PR 1 — the `--worktree` flag on OrcaArgs with its two refusals, the new `orca.tools.Worktrees` and `orca.runner.WorktreeRun`, `OrcaDir.worktreesPath`/`ensureWorktrees` with the self-ignoring `.gitignore` marker, and worktree resolution in `flow()` (not `runFlow`).
2. PR 2 — the closing summary naming the worktree path and the branch inside it, via one new `FlowSetup` field.
3. PR 3 — the shell: `FlowFlags` gains the flag, `orca run --worktree`, the interactive prompt, and the resume/session scans spanning every worktree.

Follow the plan's stated decisions rather than re-deriving them. Several were deliberately corrected during review and a fresh reading of the code will tempt you back to the wrong version: `FlowSetup` gains ONE `Option[os.Path]` field, not a directory plus a boolean; `git worktree add` needs no `--` separator and no commit-ish argument; the two shell scans TAKE the directories to scan rather than discovering them internally, so their existing temp-directory tests keep working; the resolution must live in `flow()` because `RunManifestWriter.start` is there.

Include the ADR amendments (0018 §2.5, 0019, 0021 §3/§8/§10) and the README changes the plan lists, and write the tests the plan names for each PR.

resultJson.description:
Add a run-level `--worktree` flag to orca (issue #150): at startup orca creates — or reuses — a git worktree at `<main checkout>/.orca/worktrees/<promptHash>` and runs the entire flow inside it, so several runs can work on one repository concurrently without sharing a checkout. The worktree is detached at the invoking checkout's HEAD, keyed by the same 12-hex prompt hash as the progress log (so resuming the same task lands in the same worktree), hidden from the enclosing repo by a self-ignoring `.gitignore`, and never removed by orca. The flag refuses `--skip-branch` (git won't check a branch out twice) and `--keep-changes` (uncommitted files aren't carried over) before anything is created.

The design is fully settled in docs/plans/worktree-runs/specification.md and implementation-plan.md (both in the working tree, untracked) — they are the authority; follow their decisions rather than re-deriving. The work is the plan's three PRs landed as one change on this branch: PR 1 adds the flag, the `orca.tools.Worktrees` git plumbing, `orca.runner.WorktreeRun` resolution wired into `flow()` (not `runFlow` — `RunManifestWriter.start` lives in `flow()` and must write into the resolved directory), plus `OrcaDir.worktreesPath`/`ensureWorktrees`; PR 2 makes the closing summary name the worktree path and its branch via one new `Option[os.Path]` field on `FlowSetup`; PR 3 gives the shell the flag (`orca run --worktree`, an interactive prompt) and makes the resume-interrupted-run and session-listing scans span every worktree of the repository, with the scans taking the directories to scan rather than discovering them. ADR amendments (0018 §2.5, 0019, 0021 §3/§8/§10) and README changes are included with the tasks that make the existing text untrue.

tasks.title: tools: Worktrees git plumbing and OrcaDir worktrees directory
tasks.description: New `private[orca] object Worktrees` at tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/Worktrees.scala, shelling out through `orca.subprocess.QuietProc.call`. Three operations: `mainCheckout(cwd): Option[os.Path]` — parent of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (`--path-format=absolute` is required; `None` outside a git repository); `list(cwd): List[os.Path]` — the paths from `git worktree list --porcelain` (empty outside a repo; paths only — no branch or prunable fields, nothing consumes them); `add(cwd, path)` — `git worktree add --detach <path>` with NO commit-ish (git detaches at cwd's HEAD, the specified start point) and NO `--` separator. `add`'s failure must be observable to callers (a later task maps the unborn-HEAD failure to orca's own wording). In tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala add `worktreesPath(workDir)` — passive, `root(workDir) / "worktrees"`, alongside `runsPath` (:111) — and `ensureWorktrees(workDir)` mirroring `ensureCache` (:72–78): `abortIfOrcaComponentSymlink`, `os.makeDir.all`, `writeIfAbsent(dir / ".gitignore", gitignoreContents)` — deliberately NO CACHEDIR.TAG, and the scaladoc must say why (the tag tells backup tools to skip the directory; a worktree holds unmerged work), or someone will add it for symmetry. Tests in new tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/WorktreesTest.scala: `add` then `list` round-trip in a temp git repo; `mainCheckout` from both the main checkout and a linked worktree returning the same path; a `--`-requiring path (leading `-` segment) not being read as a flag.

tasks.title: runner: --worktree flag on OrcaArgs with its two refusals
tasks.description: runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala gains `worktree: Flag = Flag()` with doc "run the flow in a git worktree of this repository instead of the current checkout". The refusals live in `OrcaArgs.parse` (:23–24), not WorktreeRun: after mainargs' `constructEither`, return `Left` for `--worktree` with `--skip-branch` (git will not check the current branch out a second time in a new worktree) and for `--worktree` with `--keep-changes` (uncommitted files stay in the invoking checkout and are not carried over). Each message names both flags and why they conflict; `from` already turns a Left into `OrcaFlowException`, so the pair fails at `OrcaArgs(args)` — before `flow()` runs, before anything touches git. Note the exact wording is reused verbatim by the shell fast path in a later task, so keep the messages self-contained. Extend runner/src/test/scala/orca/OrcaArgsTest.scala (munit FunSuite): each refusal yields a Left naming both flags; `--worktree` alone parses with `worktree.value == true`.

tasks.title: runner: WorktreeRun.resolve — derive the path, create or reuse, refuse
tasks.description: New `private[orca] object WorktreeRun` at runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/WorktreeRun.scala with a `resolve(...)` returning `Either[String, os.Path]` — the only place that knows how the path is built (the shell's resume relaunch must never re-derive it). Derivation: `Worktrees.mainCheckout` of the invoking directory; `None` → Left reusing `FlowLifecycle.abortIfNoCommits`' message wording (FlowLifecycle.scala:386–392) since with `--worktree` the not-a-repo case surfaces here instead. Path = `OrcaDir.worktreesPath(mainCheckout) / ProgressStore.hashPrompt(userPrompt)` — the identical call `ProgressStore.default` makes (flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/ProgressStore.scala:88; `private[orca]`, visible from runner), so worktree and progress log always share the hash. Cases: nothing at the path → `OrcaDir.ensureWorktrees` BEFORE `Worktrees.add` (the `.gitignore` must exist before the worktree does — without it `git add -A` in main stages an embedded repo), then add detached at the invoker's HEAD; `add` failing on an unborn HEAD → Left with `abortIfNoCommits`' wording, never git's raw error. Path is a registered worktree of this repository (present in `Worktrees.list`) → return it (this is what makes a resumed run land back where its progress log is). Path exists but is not a registered worktree (plain directory, foreign repo's worktree, a file) → Left naming the path and saying orca will not take over a directory it did not create. A `list` entry whose path no longer exists on disk (prunable, produced by `git clean -xdff`) → treat as absent; `add` prunes and recreates. Tests in new runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/WorktreeRunTest.scala: same task text derives the same path and different text a different one; reuses an existing registered worktree; refuses a plain directory at the path; treats a prunable entry as absent; writes the `.gitignore` before creating.

tasks.title: runner: resolve the worktree in flow(), end-to-end test, PR-1 docs
tasks.description: In runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala (package `orca`), when `args.worktree.value`: resolve via `WorktreeRun` after `installUncaughtExceptionHandler()` (:154) and before `RunManifestWriter.start` (:172) — the manifest writer takes `workDir` and must write into the resolved directory (this is why resolution cannot live in `runFlow`; `runFlow` changes not at all, its `workDir` stays already-resolved for every caller). Move the `flowLog.info` workDir line (:150) below resolution; it logs the resolved directory and says when it is a worktree. A resolution `Left` has no dispatcher and no manifest: print `[orca] <message>` to stderr (same treatment as the NonFatal backstop at :214–216), set `outcome = FlowOutcome.Failed`, and skip the `supervised:` block entirely — which requires hoisting `orcaLog.finish()` out of the inner finally (:223) so it still runs on that path; the trailing exit-1 check (:229) needs no change. Pass the resolved directory as `runFlow`'s `workDir`. Update `flow()`'s scaladoc: "the default is the current directory" gains the `--worktree` exception. Add the end-to-end case to runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala driving `flow(...)`, NOT `runFlow(...)` (the file already has that style at :76): work lands on a branch in the worktree, the main checkout's branch and tree are untouched, the progress log is inside the worktree, and a second run with the same task text resumes in the same worktree. Docs: README.md:63 (useful-flags sentence) and :954 (`orca run` table row) gain `--worktree`; the prose block at README.md:327–342 gains a paragraph — what a worktree run isolates, that uncommitted work does not come along, the first run pays a cold build, an editor/indexer not honouring `.gitignore` sees the second checkout, cleanup is `git worktree remove`. ADR amendments: adr/0019-project-stack-settings.md §".orca/ flips to committed-by-default" (:102–141) — directory listing gains `worktrees/`, the "ephemeral state moves under .orca/cache/" paragraph gets the stated exception (ignored but not ephemeral, deliberately outside cache/), and OrcaDir named as the marker writer; adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md §2.5 (~:344) — one dated amendment recording that a worktree run always meets the dirty-tree policy's clean case, and that `--worktree` is refused with `--skip-branch` and `--keep-changes` before setup ever runs.

tasks.title: runner: closing summary names the worktree via one FlowSetup field
tasks.description: `FlowSetup` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala:225) gains exactly ONE new field `worktree: Option[os.Path]` — not a directory plus a Boolean, and not a second `teardownSuccess` parameter — computed at the single construction site in `setup` (built at :371; `setup` already has both `args` and `workDir`) as `Option.when(args.worktree.value)(workDir)`. `ClosingSummary.lines` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/ClosingSummary.scala:35) gains a `worktree: Option[os.Path]` parameter; `None` reproduces today's output byte-for-byte so every existing case keeps passing unchanged. For `Some(path)`: the first line names both the worktree path and the branch inside it (per the specification's "telling the user where the run left them"), and the `next:` line becomes `git -C <path> diff <target>` so it works from where the user is standing — `<target>` keeps its two existing shapes (`base.short`, or `base.short..countedOn` when HEAD left the counted branch); the `-C` is the only change. `teardownSuccess` (:1147) passes `setup.worktree` at the :1190–1193 emission. The failure path prints no summary today and still doesn't. Tests in runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/: a ClosingSummary case per shape — non-worktree unchanged, worktree with changes, worktree with none; extend the PR-1 FlowLifecycleTest worktree end-to-end case to assert the emitted `Step` names the worktree.

tasks.title: shell: FlowFlags.worktree, orca run --worktree, fast-path refusals
tasks.description: `FlowFlags` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowLauncher.scala:30) gains `worktree: Boolean` — the bundle exists precisely so a new flag is one field, not another positional Boolean. Thread it through `argv` (:97–117): a `worktreeArgs` alongside `verboseArgs`/`skipBranchArgs`/`keepChangesArgs` (:108–112), appended after `--` at :117 with the others. Update all four construction sites: shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/Cli.scala:165 (from the new CLI flag), shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/Main.scala:365 and :407 (pass `false` for now — later tasks wire these), shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/AuthorAction.scala:140 (all-false stays all-false — authoring runs in a sandbox, not the user's repo). `Cli.run` (:144) gains a `worktree: Flag` next to `honorPin` (:156–160), passed into FlowFlags. In shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/RunCli.scala's `run` (:13), reject `--worktree --skip-branch` and `--worktree --keep-changes` with `ExitCodes.UsageError` before any scala-cli spawn — this saves a spawn and dependency resolution; the child's own refusal (OrcaArgs) stays the authority, so use the same wording in both places. adr/0021-orca-shell.md §10's `orca run` flag table (~:834) gains `--worktree`. Tests: shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowLauncherTest.scala — `--worktree` lands after `--` with the other flow flags; shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/cli/CliTest.scala — the flag parses, and the two fast-path refusals return `UsageError`.

tasks.title: shell: interactive worktree prompt in Run-a-flow
tasks.description: `Main.runFlow` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/Main.scala:356–372) asks for the flow, the task, then whether to create a branch (`promptCreateBranch`, :435–442). Add a worktree question AFTER it, asked ONLY when the branch answer was yes — "run in a worktree" and "run on the current branch" are the incompatible pair, so asking both independently invites the user to pick a combination orca refuses; a "no" branch answer skips the worktree question and the flag stays false. The answer feeds the `FlowFlags` built at :365. Follow `promptCreateBranch`'s shape: a `private[shell]` confirm helper so a scripted-UI test can drive it directly, `UiOutcome.Cancelled` aborting the whole for-comprehension. Tests (shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/actions/RunActionTest.scala and/or the MainTest scripted-UI style): the interactive path's worktree answer reaches the launcher's flags; declining the branch never asks the worktree question.

tasks.title: shell: resume-interrupted-run scans every worktree and relaunches into it
tasks.description: `ResumeDetector.detect` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/resume/ResumeDetector.scala:33) currently reads one directory; change it to TAKE the list of directories to scan — it must not call git internally (its existing tests seed a bare temp directory with no git repo and must keep passing for the reason they assert). Keep the newest-by-mtime rule (:62) across all directories. `InterruptedRun` (:8) gains a Boolean saying the log was found in a linked worktree. Create the small shell-side discovery helper this and the next task share: `Worktrees.list(os.pwd)` falling back to `List(os.pwd)` when it comes back empty (`Worktrees` is `private[orca]`; `orca.shell` is inside package `orca` so it's visible) — this is the Cli-scaladoc seam convention: explicit directory params, resolution at the call site. Wire it at `Main.loop`'s `ResumeDetector.detect(os.pwd)` call (:119). `Main.resumeInterruptedRun` (:386–414) then passes `worktree = true` in the FlowFlags it builds at :407 when the run was found in a worktree — the derived path takes the relaunch back to the same tree. The scaladoc at :374–384 explaining why the other flags are all-false must record this flag's DIFFERENT reason: it is not inert, it is what makes the resume land in the right tree. `ProgressScan.progressLogPaths` (flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/ProgressScan.scala:26) stays one-level-deep and must not start descending into `worktrees/` — discovery goes through git's worktree list, which also finds worktrees outside the repository. adr/0021-orca-shell.md §3 (~:160) gains the scan-every-worktree rule for the resume offer. Tests: shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/resume/ResumeDetectorTest.scala — a log in a linked worktree is detected and reported as a worktree run; the existing main-checkout cases keep passing.

tasks.title: shell: session listing spans every worktree
tasks.description: `ManifestReader.list` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ManifestReader.scala:29) currently reads one `.orca/cache/runs/`; change it to TAKE the list of directories to scan (same seam rule as ResumeDetector: no git calls inside — the existing bare-temp-directory tests keep working). Keep its per-file warning behaviour and its newest-first sort by `manifest.startedAt`, which now orders across directories. Its two callers resolve the list at their call site with the discovery helper from the resume task (`Worktrees.list` falling back to the single directory): `ContinueCli.runContinue` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/ContinueCli.scala:18–25, whose `workDir` is already an explicit test seam) and `Main.loop` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/Main.scala:115). `SessionAction.resume` already uses each manifest's recorded `workDir`, so once a session is found, reattaching works without further change. adr/0021-orca-shell.md §8 (~:399) gains the spanning rule for the session listing; also check README's interactive-shell walkthrough — no second README change is needed beyond it, and only if it enumerates the run prompts. Tests: shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ManifestReaderTest.scala — manifests from two worktrees appear in one listing, newest-first across both; existing cases unchanged.

resultJson.brief:
## Read first
- docs/plans/worktree-runs/specification.md and docs/plans/worktree-runs/implementation-plan.md — untracked, in the working tree. They are the authority for every decision; read both before implementing any task. Line refs there were verified against master@c0dad27a and still hold (the branch only adds orca's own progress-log commit).
- CLAUDE.md mandates invoking the `direct-style-scala` skill (via the Skill tool) before writing or reviewing any Scala code — do that first.

## Deliberately-corrected decisions (do NOT re-derive; a fresh code reading will tempt you to the wrong version)
- `FlowSetup` gains ONE `worktree: Option[os.Path]` field — not a directory plus a Boolean, not a second `teardownSuccess` parameter.
- `git worktree add --detach <path>` takes NO `--` separator and NO commit-ish; git detaches at the invoking cwd's HEAD, which is exactly the specified start point.
- `ResumeDetector.detect` and `ManifestReader.list` TAKE the list of directories to scan; they must not call `git worktree list` internally — their existing tests seed bare temp directories (no git repo) and must keep passing. A small shell-side helper (`Worktrees.list(os.pwd)`, falling back to `List(os.pwd)` when empty) resolves the list at the `Main`/`Cli` call sites.
- Worktree resolution lives in `flow()`, not `runFlow` — `RunManifestWriter.start` (flow.scala:172) is in `flow()` and takes `workDir`; resolving later would write session manifests into the invoking checkout. `runFlow`'s `workDir` stays already-resolved for every caller.

## Modules (sbt multi-project; dependency order tools → flow → runner → shell)
- `tools/` — `orca.OrcaDir` (`.orca/` layout) and low-level plumbing (`orca.subprocess.QuietProc`). New `Worktrees` goes here: worktree ops were deleted from `GitTool` in the 2026-08 review because no flow can use them; resolution runs before any tool exists.
- `flow/` — `orca.progress.{ProgressStore, ProgressScan}`. `ProgressStore.hashPrompt` (ProgressStore.scala:88) is `private[orca]`: first 12 hex chars of SHA-256(prompt); `runner` is package `orca` so it's visible without change.
- `runner/` — `orca.OrcaArgs`, `orca.flow`/`runFlow` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala — NOTE: package `orca`, the plan calls it "runner/.../flow.scala"), `orca.runner.FlowLifecycle`, `orca.runner.ClosingSummary`. New `WorktreeRun` goes here (run-level policy).
- `shell/` — interactive shell + CLI: `orca.shell.Main`, `cli/Cli.scala`, `cli/RunCli.scala`, `cli/ContinueCli.scala`, `run/FlowLauncher.scala` (`FlowFlags`), `resume/ResumeDetector.scala`, `sessions/ManifestReader.scala`, `actions/AuthorAction.scala`. `orca.shell` is inside package `orca`, so `private[orca]` members (Worktrees, OrcaDir) are visible.

## Key existing code (verified line refs)
- OrcaDir (tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala): `private val gitignoreContents = "# Automatically created by orca.\n*\n"` (:12); `ensureCache` pattern to mirror at :72–78 (`abortIfOrcaComponentSymlink`, `os.makeDir.all`, `writeIfAbsent(dir/".gitignore", ...)`, plus CACHEDIR.TAG which worktrees deliberately OMIT — say why in scaladoc or someone adds it for symmetry); passive `runsPath` at :111 (`worktreesPath` sits alongside as `root(workDir) / "worktrees"`); `writeIfAbsent` handles the create race (:168).
- QuietProc (tools/src/main/scala/orca/subprocess/QuietProc.scala): `QuietProc.call(args: Seq[String], cwd: os.Path = os.pwd, ...): os.CommandResult` — captured stdout/stderr, `check = false`, caller inspects `exitCode`/`out`/`err`. Convention: production tool code never calls raw `os.proc` (ConfigSummary.branchLine does, but it's shell-side legacy — use QuietProc).
- OrcaArgs (runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala): mainargs case class; `parse(args): Either[String, OrcaArgs]` at :23–24 wraps `constructEither`; `from` turns Left into `OrcaFlowException`. Add refusals by flat-mapping parse's Right.
- flow() (runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala:120–229): `orcaLog = OrcaLog.start()` :147, `flowLog.info("orca {} starting (workDir={})")` :150, `installUncaughtExceptionHandler()` :154, `supervised:` :168, `RunManifestWriter.start(workDir, ...)` :172 (NOT inside any try today — throwing before it escapes uncaught), NonFatal backstop prints `[orca] <msg>` :214–216, inner `finally` runs `manifestWriter.finish` / `costTracker.printSummary()` / `orcaLog.finish()` :217–223, `if outcome == FlowOutcome.Failed then System.exit(1)` :229. Left-path shape per plan: print `[orca] <message>`, `outcome = FlowOutcome.Failed`, skip the whole `supervised:` block, hoist `orcaLog.finish()` out of the inner finally so it still runs.
- FlowLifecycle (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala): `case class FlowSetup(store, featureBranch, startBranch, stackSettings, branchMode, untrackedOnFailure, startingCommit)` :225–233; `setup(args, agent, git, workDir, ...)` :297–379 builds it at :371 — the ONE site to compute `Option.when(args.worktree.value)(workDir)`; `abortIfNoCommits` :386–392 (message: "orca needs a git repository with at least one commit — initialize one if needed (git init), then make the first commit (git add -A && git commit -m \"initial commit\")") — reuse this wording for WorktreeRun's not-a-repo/unborn-HEAD Lefts; `teardownSuccess(git, setup, returnToStartBranch, emit)` :1147 emits `ClosingSummary.lines(git.currentBranch(), changes)` per line as `OrcaEvent.Step` at :1190–1193.
- ClosingSummary (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/ClosingSummary.scala:35): `def lines(branch: String, changes: Option[RunChanges]): List[String]`; shapes: `done — you are on branch '$branch'` alone / + `no files changed` / + `$files file(s) changed since ${base.short}` + `next: git diff <target>` where `<target>` is `base.short` or `${base.short}..$countedOn`. Worktree form: first line names path AND branch inside it; `next: git -C <path> diff <target>` (the `-C` is the only change to target). `None` must reproduce today's output byte-for-byte.
- FlowLauncher (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowLauncher.scala): `case class FlowFlags(verbose, skipBranch, keepChanges)` :30; `argv(flow, orcaVersion, task, flags, workspaceDir)` :97–117 builds `Seq("scala-cli","run",...) ++ ... ++ Seq("--", task) ++ verboseArgs ++ skipBranchArgs ++ keepChangesArgs` — flow flags land AFTER `--` (:108–117). Four FlowFlags construction sites: Cli.scala:165, Main.scala:365 (interactive run), Main.scala:407 (resume relaunch), AuthorAction.scala:140 (all-false, stays all-false — sandbox).
- Cli (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/Cli.scala): `run` @main at :144–173, flags `verbose`/`skipBranch`/`keepChanges`/`honorPin` as mainargs `Flag`; `ExitCodes.UsageError = 2`. RunCli.run (cli/RunCli.scala:13) is where the shell fast-path refusals go (before `Cli.withTerminal`/spawn) — same wording as OrcaArgs' refusals; the child stays the authority.
- Main (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/Main.scala): `loop` calls `ManifestReader.list(os.pwd, ManifestReader.pidAlive)` :115 and `ResumeDetector.detect(os.pwd)` :119; `runFlow` :356–372 prompts flow → task → `promptCreateBranch` :435–442 (confirm, default yes; `UiOutcome.Cancelled → None`), builds FlowFlags at :365; `resumeInterruptedRun` :386–414 builds all-false FlowFlags at :407 — its scaladoc (:374–384) explains why all-false is correct; the new worktree flag has a DIFFERENT reason (it's what makes the relaunch land back in the right tree) and that must be recorded there. `promptCreateBranch` is the shape to copy for the worktree prompt (private[shell], scripted-UI testable).
- ResumeDetector (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/resume/ResumeDetector.scala): `case class InterruptedRun(flowName, userPrompt)` :8; `detect(workDir): Option[InterruptedRun]` :33 — newest by `os.mtime` via `ProgressScan.progressLogPaths(workDir)` :62; all failures silent (runs on every menu redraw).
- ManifestReader (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ManifestReader.scala): `list(workDir, pidAlive: Long => Boolean): (List[RecordedRun], List[String])` :29 — reads `OrcaDir.runsPath(workDir)` passively, per-file warnings, newest-first by `manifest.startedAt`. Callers: ContinueCli.runContinue (cli/ContinueCli.scala:18–25, `workDir` already an explicit test seam) and Main.loop:115. `SessionAction.resume` uses each manifest's recorded workDir — reattaching needs no change.
- ProgressScan (flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/ProgressScan.scala:26): lists `.orca/` one level deep, filters to files matching `progress-[0-9a-f]{12}\.json` — correct that it never descends into `worktrees/`; must stay that way.

## Verified git behaviour (git 2.53, from the plan — rely on these)
`git worktree add --detach <abs-path>` with no commit-ish detaches at the invoker's HEAD; nested `.orca/worktrees/<hash>` location is allowed without warning; without the `.gitignore`, `git add -A` in main stages the worktree as an embedded-repo gitlink (the marker is load-bearing → `ensureWorktrees` must run BEFORE `add`); orca's own `:(exclude).orca/*` commits never stage it either way; `git clean -xdff` leaves a `prunable` admin entry whose path is gone — a `list` entry with a nonexistent path is treated as absent and `add` prunes+recreates; `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` names `<main>/.git` from main AND from any linked worktree (`--path-format=absolute` is required — the bare form is relative to the main checkout).

## Conventions, build, tests
- Scala 3 braceless style; munit `FunSuite` with `test("..."):` syntax (see runner/src/test/scala/orca/OrcaArgsTest.scala). Existing suites to extend all exist at the paths the plan names; new files: tools/.../WorktreesTest.scala, runner/.../WorktreeRunTest.scala.
- Build: `sbt compile`, `sbt test`, `sbt "runner/testOnly orca.runner.WorktreeRunTest"`, `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Warnings (-Wunused:all, -Wvalue-discard, -Wnonunit-statement) aren't fatal but must be fixed. sbt runs take a long time (8–15 min for full test); run them in the foreground and wait.
- Gotcha: if suddenly every command exits 1, /tmp (tmpfs) is full — clean `/tmp/orca-*` first.
- Visibility: `private[orca]` for cross-module internals (Worktrees, WorktreeRun, OrcaDir additions), `private[shell]`/`private[cli]` on the shell side. Errors at boundaries as `Either[String, X]`; `OrcaFlowException` for aborts.
- Test seams: explicit `workDir`/directory-list parameters, never `os.pwd` read inside logic (Cli's scaladoc states this as the convention).
- Scaladoc on non-obvious publics: usage/invariants, never implementation narration. Code comments only where non-trivial reasoning is needed; keep all prose maximally short. Never commit; the enclosing orca flow handles commits.
- FlowLifecycleTest already drives both `flow(...)` (at :76) and `runFlow(...)`; the worktree e2e case MUST use `flow(...)` — resolution lives there.
- Docs targets: README.md:63 (useful-flags sentence), :327–342 (lifecycle prose block), :954 (`orca run` table row). ADRs: adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md §2.5 (~:344), adr/0019-project-stack-settings.md §".orca/ flips to committed-by-default" (:102–141), adr/0021-orca-shell.md §3 (~:160), §8 (~:399), §10 flag table (~:834).
